approval_contract: Each approved case must include reviewer evidence for wire coverage, line width, tip positions and absence of logical flywires. Source structure checks alone are not approval.
method: Rendered each page as green=wire supervision, blue=pin tips, yellow=ignore, plus a second overlay marking large unlabelled ink in red. Compared both against the rendered drawing. Quantitative cross-checks: share of label pixels within 1 px of ink, label-pixel distance percentiles, and the grey level of nearby ink.

0001.render_style: black/green wire strokes, coloured net labels
0001.visual: labelled segments sit on the drawn wires across the RP2350 core, radio module, flash and PSRAM sections; tips land on component terminals
0001.caveats: page frame ruler and title block are not wires and are correctly unlabelled; a few short leads at IC pins are outside the wire labels

0018.render_style: black symbol bodies, green wire strokes
0018.visual: decoupling networks, crystal, LED, LDO and header wires are labelled; symbol outlines inside the STM32 block are not and should not be
0018.caveats: dense IC body leaves most of the ink unlabelled by design; tip positions trace the pin stubs

0022.visual: every green interconnect of the 4x4 switch matrix and the J5 connector is covered; tips sit at the switch terminals

0080.render_style: green wire strokes, black symbols, dense page
0080.visual: labelled wires follow the drawing; nothing contradicts the supervision at page scale
0080.caveats: densest validation page (265 tips); label recall is the risk, not alignment. Per-page wire F1 with the A3 model is 0.627, the lowest of the dense set

0102.render_style: red symbol/component drawing, green wires only
0102.visual: green interconnect is labelled; the red symbol-internal nets and outlines are not, which is a rendering convention rather than a label gap
0102.caveats: least aligned page of the ten (82.3%); the low share is dominated by symbol-internal red drawing, not by missing wires

0131.render_style: red frame and symbols, green wires
0131.visual: the MT3520B buck converter and its feedback divider are fully covered; only the page frame and title block stay unlabelled
0131.caveats: sparse page: 5055 wire pixels, so a few pixels move the percentage a lot

0149.render_style: red frame and symbols, green wires
0149.visual: TX4137 buck converter wiring labelled end to end; the red parts list text block and page frame stay unlabelled
0149.caveats: sparsest validation page; also carries a large red text block that is not a wire

0170.render_style: red frame and symbols, green wires
0170.visual: densest tip page that still has clean wire geometry; interconnect coverage looks complete
0170.caveats: 251 tips; model-side pin recall is the limiting factor, not the labels

0208.render_style: three panels of medium-grey strokes (about 183 grey) inside a large page
0208.visual: labels follow the panel wiring; alignment is the weakest of the ten because the strokes are light and the page frame contributes dark ink
0208.caveats: approved as label-valid, but the current model outputs no wire or pin probability above threshold on this page (F1 = 0). This is a documented unreachable page, not a label defect; see reports/page_0208_diagnosis.md

0224.render_style: dark strokes, red component symbols, green wires
0224.visual: tone-control network fully covered; tips on the op-amp and passive terminals

coverage_plan.why: approval is for evidence, not for training: v2 training used all 238 draft train pages regardless, and approved_cases only gates whether a run may claim reviewed labels

what_approval_does_not_establish: that the letters/values/pin names on these pages are correct (only geometry was reviewed)
that the model reaches acceptable accuracy - this record separates label quality from model quality
any official competition score; official_NetF1 and ComponentF1 remain unavailable
review_artifacts: D:/pcb_unet_v2/reports/label_reviews/<case>.png (green wire / blue tip / yellow ignore) and D:/pcb_unet_v2/reports/approval_<case>_coverage.png (green labelled, red large unlabelled ink)
